faq.a: Ibrahem is associated with the Arabic form إبراهيم, whose core sense is ibrahim; the qur'anic form of abraham.

faq.q: What is the origin of Ibrahem?
faq.a: Ibrahem is associated with Arabic. Ibrahem is a variant transliteration of Arabic إِبْرَاهِيم (Ibrāhīm), the Qur'anic form of Abraham. The source gloss 'Father of many nations' is unsupported; the name is a proper name. Same name as ibrah, ibraheem, ibrahim and ibrhim.
Yes — the underlying form إبراهيم is Arabic.
Ibrahem can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Ibrahem mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ibrahem is rendered ابراهیم and carries the sense ابراهیم، صورت قرآنی ابراهیم.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ibrahem, ibrahem. Script forms are إبراهيم, ابراهیم, ابراہیم, इब्राहीम.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
